valuationInputs.name: Beta
valuationInputs.reason: 8 steps, 17 Nov 2026. (1) Business: one business in effect, renewable power generation (Uganda hydro, Sri Lankan mini-hydro, solar, dendro) sold under long-term contracts to the national grid operators; engineering and plantation are small. So one sector beta. (2) Damodaran's emerging-markets dataset (betaEmerg) couldn't be opened from this run. Stand-in from a web-search extract of his global table (January 2026): Green & Renewable Energy unlevered, cash-corrected 0.57 (258 firms); Power is 0.46. The renewable figure is used. (3) Relevered with net debt Rs 6.85bn (30 Sep 2026) / market value Rs 22.79bn (955.8mn voting at Rs 22.10 + 82.1mn non-voting at Rs 20.30, 30 Sep 2026) = 0.30 and 25% tax: 0.57 x (1 + 0.75 x 0.30) = 0.70. (4) Local 5-year betas: only one found, StockAnalysis 0.28 (5Y, web-search extract); Simply Wall St shows 0.27 for the non-voting share (period not shown); TradingView 0.30 is a 1-year beta and is ignored. Fewer than 3 sources, so step 4 can't be completed; the share also trades thinly. (5) Higher of 0.70 and 0.28 = 0.70. (6) Within 0.3-2. (7) Into the formula by scripts/reinvestment.py. Provisional: refresh in January 2027 with Damodaran's emerging-markets file and three verified local 5-year betas. Uganda's own country risk isn't added, although about two-thirds of profit comes from there. 18 Nov 2026 (/redo full): Damodaran's site was blocked from this run as well; inputs unchanged. Relevered at Rs 22.00 (CSE close 18 Nov 2026): net debt 6.85 / market value about 22.6bn = 0.30, still 0.70.

valuationInputs.name: WACC
valuationInputs.reason: From scripts/reinvestment.py (18 Nov 2026): cost of debt 9.56% (interest paid 0.364 ÷ average borrowings and leases 3.81, FY2026), tax 25.1%, debt weight 23.1% (net debt Rs 6.85bn at Sep 2026, market cap Rs 22.83bn at Rs 22.00).

valuationInputs.name: Growth check
valuationInputs.value: Assumed 3% / 6% / 9%; supported 32.8% (reinvestment rate 197.7% × return on capital 16.6%, FY2026). All within 2 pts. The supported rate is inflated by one build year (21 MW of solar, capex Rs 2.73bn against depreciation of Rs 0.44bn), so the assumptions stay well below it.
valuationInputs.reason: From scripts/reinvestment.py on the FY2026 figures.

valuationInputs.name: Growth
valuationInputs.value: Bear 3% then 3% / Base 6% then 4% / Bull 9% then 5%
valuationInputs.reason: Five years, then long-run, below the 12.24% bond yield and WACC; long-run reinvestment = growth ÷ return on capital.

valuationInputs.name: After-tax operating profit (start)
valuationInputs.value: Bear Rs 1.30bn / Base Rs 1.48bn / Bull Rs 1.69bn
valuationInputs.reason: Operating profit excluding JVs Rs 1.85 / 2.05 / 2.25bn (FY2026 1.955; H1 FY2027 about 1.0 without the unexplained 0.245 other income; new Gurugoda and Ranna capacity) × (1 − 30% / 28% / 25%).

valuationInputs.name: Maintenance capex basis
valuationInputs.reason: No company split. The calculator's range (1.43 / 0.77 / 0.44) is distorted by the FY2026 build year; base = current depreciation run-rate (H1 FY2027 × 2), bull = FY2026 depreciation, bear about 1.4x depreciation.

valuationInputs.name: Cash after maintenance capex (start)
valuationInputs.value: Bear Rs 1.10bn / Base Rs 1.48bn / Bull Rs 1.80bn
valuationInputs.reason: After-tax operating profit + depreciation of about 0.55 − maintenance.

valuationInputs.name: JVs and projects per share
valuationInputs.reason: JVs Rs 2.434bn and other project investments Rs 2.209bn (mainly Storex) at Sep 2026, less minorities Rs 0.265bn: bear 85% / 80% of book, base book, bull JVs 1.35x and projects 1.5x cost.

valuationInputs.name: Long-run ROE
valuationInputs.reason: Reported ROE 15–19% over five years; 16.1% in FY2026. Residual income moves ROE from 16% to these levels over ten years (scripts/valuation.py), so the bear case fades rather than drops at once (changed 18 Nov).

valuationInputs.name: EPS to March 2027 × P/E
valuationInputs.reason: H1 EPS about Rs 0.65 on all shares. Forward justified P/E at the cost of equity as scripts/valuation.py computes it (payout ÷ (r − g), without the extra (1 + g) used by hand on 17 Nov). Base is 10.6% below the Rs 1.51 run-rate (last 12 months) because that includes Rs 0.245bn of unexplained other income and finance costs have doubled.

valuationInputs.name: Dividend 2026/27
valuationInputs.reason: After the five growth years the payout becomes 1 − long-run growth ÷ ROE (Damodaran's two-stage dividend model): 78.6% / 75.0% / 70.6%, from long-run growth 3/4/5% and long-run ROE 14/16/17% (the 'Long-run ROE' input), on EPS 1.15/1.35/1.5 (the 'EPS to March 2027 × P/E' input). Corrected 2026-11-21: before, the code kept the high-growth payout forever. Earlier reason: Rs 0.20 interim so far (Rs 0.35 a year earlier); Rs 0.65 for 2025/26. Bull growth cut from 9% to 8% on 18 Nov to stay below the 8.9% supported by kept profit × ROE (55.2% × 16.1%).

valuationInputs.name: Methods used
valuationInputs.value: Whole-company DCF + JVs and projects, P/E, justified P/B, residual income, dividends
valuationInputs.reason: A contracted power producer suits a DCF; equity-accounted JVs and the battery storage stake added separately. All five methods come from scripts/valuation.py (modelInputs). From 18 Nov 2026 (second redo) the DCF + stakes is saved as modelInputs.dcf with the stakes as dcf.addOn (Rs 3.44 / 4.22 / 6.10 a share), so the What if? panel can recalculate it.
